title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This consolidated standards document defines Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards across APIs, coding, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, performance, and the use of Architecture Decision Records (ADRs). It is a curated reference for engineers, architects, and platform owners to ensure consistent design, operational safety, and predictable economics in production.

Scope

Applies to: all new and existing services under the Redwood runtime and control plane, SDKs, public APIs, Dedicated infrastructure, and Private deployment packaging. Exceptions require an ADR and explicit approval from the owning team and the Architecture Guild.

1) API Standards

- Style: RESTful first-class endpoints for service-to-service control plane; OpenAPI v3 for public endpoints and internal client generation. Use JSON for payloads and UTF-8 encoded strings.
- Versioning: Path versioning (/v1/, /v2/). Backwards-compatible additions do not require a new major version. Breaking changes require a deprecation window (>=90 days) and communication plan.
- Pagination: use keyset pagination by default (cursor, limit). Avoid offset for high-cardinality resources.
- Rate-limiting headers: include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Return 429 with Retry-After for throttling.
- Error model: standard error envelope {"code":"SHORT_CODE","message":"user-facing message","details":{}}. HTTP mapping: 400/401/403/404/409/429/500. Provide machine-readable codes for retries/idempotency guidance.
- Idempotency: POST endpoints that create resources must support an Idempotency-Key header. Duplicate detection window: 24h unless stated.
- Streaming: server-sent events / chunked Transfer-Encoding for token streaming in generation APIs with clear reconnection semantics.
- OpenAPI snippet (example):
  "openapi: 3.0.1
  paths:
    /v1/generate:
      post:
        x-service: inference
        responses:
          '200': {description: 'OK'}"

API Review Checklist (for PRs):
1. OpenAPI spec updated and validated.
2. Consumer compatibility considered (migration plan for breaking changes).
3. Rate limits, quotas, and billing metadata included.
4. Security review: auth scopes and least privilege.

2) Coding Standards

- Languages: Go for core services (control plane), Rust/C++ for latency-critical runtime components, Python for data/ML tooling.
- Linters and formatters: gofmt/golangci-lint for Go, rustfmt/clippy for Rust, black/flake8 for Python. Enforce in CI.
- Testing: unit tests >= 80% coverage for business logic; integration tests for API contracts; fuzz tests for parsers and input handling.
- Types & Contracts: prefer explicit types and strong typing at service boundaries. Use generated clients from OpenAPI and protobuf when available.
- PR guidelines: keep PRs < 400 lines when possible; include design summary, testing plan, and rollout steps for infra or API changes.
- Commit message format: <scope>(<component>): <short description>

3) Infrastructure Standards

- IaC: Terraform modules central in repo 'infra-modules'. Modules must be versioned and published to internal registry. Changes to core modules require a pass in the Terraform module review channel and an ADR if breaking.
- Networking: VPC per-customer for Private deployments; subnets and AZ spread for Dedicated pools. Default deny security groups; explicit egress rules.
- Identity & Keys: use customer/cluster KMS keys for encryption-at-rest. Secrets stored in Vault with per-team scopes.
- Tagging and Billing: all resources must include tags: team, service, environment, cost-center, owner-email.
- Backup & DR: RPO: 1h for critical control-plane state; RTO: 2h for control-plane services. Runbook pointers required in module docs.

Infrastructure Configuration Table (minimum required tags and settings):
| key | required? | example |
| team | yes | "inference-runtime" | 
| environment | yes | "prod" | 
| owner-email | yes | "infra-owner@redwood.ai" |
| kms_key | conditional | "projects/..../keys/runtime" |

4) Model-serving Standards

- Packaging: model artifacts must include manifest.json with schema_version, model_id, framework, quantization_profile (if any), and checksums. Support for ONNX/torchscript/ggml and custom runtime bundles.
- Versioning: immutable model versions. Model id + semver-like version. Deployments reference pinned model versions; automated rollouts may point to version aliases.
- Rollouts & Safety: default rollout strategy = canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic quality gates. Quality gates: error rate, latency, and eval prompt-set quality metrics.
- Quantization: maintain two artifacts where possible: float (for quality baseline) + quantized (for cost). Verify regressions against baseline eval set before promoting quantized variant.
- Fallbacks: on OOM/timeout/failure, route to a compatible model variant (lower memory or CPU variant) with graceful degradation messaging.
- Input validation: enforce length limits, tokenization guards, and anti-injection sanitizers at the edge.

Model Deployment Checklist:
1. Model manifest and checksum present.
2. Evaluations passed (regression <= configured threshold).
3. Rollout stages defined and automated.
4. Observability hooks (metrics/tail-sampling) enabled.

5) Observability Standards

- Telemetry: metrics (Prometheus), traces (OpenTelemetry), structured logs (JSON) shipped to centralized observability stack.
- Metrics naming conventions: service_<component>_<metric>_{total|seconds|gauge}. Use labels: service, route, model_id, env, region.
- Mandatory metrics: request_count, request_errors, request_latency_seconds_bucket, tokens_generated_total, kv_cache_hit_ratio.
- Tracing: sample 100% of error traces and 1% of successful traces by default; adjustable per-service. Include trace context in logs.
- Dashboards: per-route latency and cost dashboard; per-model quality dashboard (eval regressions, hallucination signals).
- Alerts & SLOs: alerts are for actionable operational events only. Escalation paths documented in runbooks.

Alerting thresholds (recommended starting points):
- Route 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> Page on-call.
- P99 latency > 2x target for 5m -> Page on-call.
- KV cache hit ratio drop > 20% vs baseline for 15m -> Pager (possible cache invalidation).

6) Performance Standards and SLOs

Global SLOs (examples — teams may tighten per-route):
- Latency targets (inference requests): p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms for small models on Dedicated GPU pool. Hosted endpoints will have route-specific profiles documented in the model catalog.
- Availability: 99.9% uptime for control plane APIs; 99.5% for hosted inference depending on tier.
- Error budget policy: when monthly error budget exhausted for a service, freeze non-essential feature rollouts and schedule reliability fixes.

Autoscaling guidance:
- Scale-up trigger: sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for 5m or queue length > preconfigured threshold.
- Scale-down: utilization < 30% for 10m with cool-down 10m.

Perf testing checklist:
1. Benchmark with representative prompt mixes (short, long, streaming).
2. Verify batching behaves correctly under target QPS.
3. Run tail-latency analysis and kernel contention profiling.

7) Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

- Purpose: document important architectural choices, alternatives considered, and consequences. ADRs must be short, time-stamped, and linked to implementation PRs and runbooks.
- ADR template (required fields): id, title, status (proposed|accepted|deprecated), context, decision, consequences, date, owners.
- ADR lifecycle: proposed -> review (Architecture Guild + owners) -> accepted -> implemented -> linked in confluence and codebase. Deprecated ADRs must include reason and migration notes.

Example ADRs to reference:
- ADR-2025-11: Unified API versioning strategy (accepted)
- ADR-2026-01: Runtime kernel selection approach (accepted)

Governance and Ownership

- Architecture Guild: cross-functional reviewers for major ADRs and standards updates.
- Owners: each section above has a primary owning team (listed below). Owners are responsible for keeping docs and checklists current.
  - API Standards: eng-developer-experience
  - Coding Standards: eng-platform
  - Infrastructure Standards: eng-infra
  - Model-serving Standards: eng-serving-runtime
  - Observability Standards: eng-platform + eng-sre
  - Performance SLOs: eng-sre + eng-serving-runtime

Change process
1. Propose change as PR against this document in the confluence-docs repo.
2. Create ADR for breaking or long-lived decisions.
3. Run automated link and checklist validation in CI.
4. Publish once reviewers from Architecture Guild approve.

Appendix: Templates and Examples

- ADR template (text):
  ID: ADR-YYYY-NNN
  Title: short title
  Status: proposed/accepted/deprecated
  Date: YYYY-MM-DD
  Context: ...
  Decision: ...
  Consequences: ...
  Owners: team(s)

- Model manifest example (JSON):
  {
    "schema_version": "1.0",
    "model_id": "lama-13b",
    "framework": "torch",
    "quantization_profile": "q4_0",
    "checksum": "sha256:..."
  }
